current_fields.retired_by_action: Find, for ANY chemically-induced transcriptional-proximity system, a relationship between a CHARACTERISED induced interface (size, cooperativity, or induced-complex residence time) and transcriptional output — MISSING-3. ⛔ Measured 2026-08-07 at $0 by reading the committed full text of the route's own motivating source on the literature-cache branch: `cooperativ*` 0 occurrences, `linker` 0, `contact residue` 0, `interface` only inside a reference title, and no structure of the induced complex. That source characterises the ternary complex functionally and not structurally, so it does not supply the input. Supporting Information was not in the cache and is the one place left to look before this escalates to requires_wet_lab. Until then REQ-TCIP-2 (report at both floors, assert only what holds at both) is the route's operative requirement.

proposed_fields.retired_by: A deposited, characterised induced interface in a chemically-induced TRANSCRIPTIONAL-proximity system was found and MEASURED under the reach sampler's own contact predicate: PDB 9MZA, 'Chemically Hijacked BCL6-TCIP3-p300 Complex', X-ray 2.1 A, released 2025-04-16, whose own rcsb_primary_citation names Nix et al., 'A Bivalent Molecular Glue Linking Lysine Acetyltransferases to Oncogene-induced Cell Death' (bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.03.14.643404 -> Cell 10.1016/j.cell.2026.06.037, PMID 42476129). The induced BCL6-p300 interface measures FAR BELOW the degrader-derived floor the route inherited, in both directions and in both crystallographically independent copies. The floor is therefore bounded from above by real data, and the sign question the owner document recorded as unknown answers 'smaller'. Numbers: research/modalities/nr4a3-induced-interface-census.json. Reasoning, provenance and limits: research/manuscripts/tcip/tcip-interface-floor-sizing.md.
proposed_fields.residual_open_question: NOT this blocker, and narrower than it: no SERIES exists — two or more induced interfaces of different size in one transcriptional system with matched transcriptional output — which is what would turn a bound into a calibration curve.
